caption: A handful of chocolate chips is dropped into a saucepan of hot cream, and the chips melt into the cream.

sa.check: Chocolate chips are dropped into the cream.
The chips melt: they lose their shape.
Dark streaks spread through the pale cream.
The drop comes first and the melting follows.

pc.expect: The chips only soften, lose their edges and shrink while the cream grows darker; chips do not form again.
pc.fail: A chip regains its pointed shape; or dark streaks gather back into a chip; or the mixture separates into pale cream and hard chips again; or the chips alternate between hard and soft.

pc.expect: The melting chocolate is a thick liquid that smears and blends into the cream and the chips are soft solids that squash rather than shatter.
pc.fail: A chip shatters into dry shards; or the melted chocolate runs as thin as water and sits apart on top; or a chip stays hard-edged while glossy and smearing; or the mixture sets into a rigid block in the hot pan.

pc.expect: The chips sink into the cream or sit in it and the dark streaks sink and spread; the cream's surface stays level.
pc.fail: A chip rises out of the cream and hangs above it; or the streaks climb the pan's wall and stay; or the surface tilts and stays tilted with the pan level; or chocolate gathers on the pan's rim.

pc.expect: The chips show the hot cream around them: they go glossy where they are wetted and the cream darkens where they lie.
pc.fail: The chips sit in the cream sharp-edged and matt while the cream darkens; or the cream darkens on the far side of the pan from the chips with nothing stirring it there; or the chips soften while the cream stays pale everywhere.

pc.expect: The chips that go in are the chips in the pan and the pan's contents gain nothing.
pc.fail: Chips appear in the pan with none falling in; or a chip vanishes with none of it joining the cream; or the pan's level rises with nothing added; or a chip passes through the pan's wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pan, the hob and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.
